originalTitle: Trump says U.S. has sold more than $13 billion of Venezuela oil since Maduro's capture
summary: President Donald Trump said Monday the U.S. has sold more than $13 billion of Venezuelan oil since taking control of the South American nation's energy exports.
content:
President Donald Trump said Monday that the U.S. has collected more than $13 billion from the sale of Venezuelan crude oil since the overthrow of former President Nicolás Maduro.

The U.S. seized control of Venezuela's oil exports after capturing Maduro in a military raid on Jan. 3. Trump was responding to a question about a Financial Times ' report that estimated how much money his administration had collected from the sales.

"$13 billion from Venezuela? I think even more than that," the president told reporters aboard Air Force One as he traveled to Michigan to tour a General Motors' facility. "We've paid for that war many times over."

Trump said the money is used to run Venezuela. "We're taking in a lot of money — billions and billions of dollars from Venezuela," Trump said.

The U.S. has largely left the Venezuelan government in place after ousting Maduro. Washington has been closely cooperating with interim President Delcy Rodríguez, who served as vice president under Maduro.

Democrats in Congress have pressed the administration to disclose how much money it has collected from the sales, how the funds are spent, and how the program is monitored.

Energy Secretary Chris Wright told Semafor in an April interview that the U.S. had sold around 150 million barrels of Venezuelan oil since January.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio told Congress in June that the oil sales are audited by KPMG. The money is held in a Citibank account, Rubio said.

"It's an ongoing audit, so it's not a once-a-year audit, it's on every expenditure, every single disbursement is audited by KPMG," Rubio told Congress.

The Trump administration initially deposited $500 million in sales to an account in Qatar that was controlled by the U.S. government, Wright said in February. The U.S. subsequently set up a Treasury account and stopped sending money to the Qatar account, he said.

State Department official Michael Kozak told Congress in April that around $3 billion had been disbursed from the Treasury account. Kozak said the money was used to pay the salaries of Venezuela's government workers, buy supplies for the nation's oil industry and other approved uses.

Rubio authorizes the disbursement of the funds under an executive order issued by Trump on Jan. 9. The president's order states that the money is the property of the Venezuelan government held in a custodial capacity by the U.S.
chineseTitle: 特朗普称自马杜罗被捕以来美国已向委内瑞拉出售了价值超过130亿美元的石油
chineseSummary: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周一表示，自控制这个南美国家的能源出口以来，美国已向委内瑞拉出售了价值超过 130 亿美元的石油。
chineseContent:
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周一表示，自前总统尼古拉斯·马杜罗被推翻以来，美国已通过出售委内瑞拉原油获得了超过 130 亿美元的收入。

1 月 3 日，美国在军事突袭中抓获马杜罗后，控制了委内瑞拉的石油出口。特朗普当时是在回答有关《金融时报》报道的问题，该报道估计了他的政府从石油销售中收取了多少钱。

“来自委内瑞拉的 130 亿美元？我认为甚至更多，”总统在前往密歇根州参观通用汽车工厂时在空军一号上对记者说道。 “我们已经多次为这场战争付出了代价。”

特朗普表示，这笔钱将用于管理委内瑞拉。特朗普说：“我们从委内瑞拉获得了大量资金——数十亿美元。”

推翻马杜罗后，美国基本上让委内瑞拉政府继续留任。华盛顿一直与在马杜罗领导下担任副总统的临时总统德尔西·罗德里格斯密切合作。

国会中的民主党人敦促政府披露从销售中筹集了多少钱、资金如何使用以及如何监控该计划。

能源部长克里斯·赖特 (Chris Wright) 在 4 月份的一次采访中告诉 Semafor，自 1 月份以来，美国已出售了约 1.5 亿桶委内瑞拉石油。

国务卿马可·卢比奥 (Marco Rubio) 6 月份告诉国会，石油销售由毕马威会计师事务所 (KPMG) 进行审计。卢比奥说，这笔钱存放在花旗银行账户中。

卢比奥告诉国会：“这是一项持续的审计，所以不是每年一次的审计，而是每一项支出、每一项支出都由毕马威会计师事务所审计。”

赖特二月份表示，特朗普政府最初将 5 亿美元的销售额存入由美国政府控制的卡塔尔账户。他说，美国随后设立了一个财政部账户，并停止向卡塔尔账户汇款。

国务院官员迈克尔·科扎克 (Michael Kozak) 4 月份告诉国会，财政部账户已支出约 30 亿美元。科扎克表示，这笔钱用于支付委内瑞拉政府工作人员的工资、为国家石油工业购买物资以及其他经批准的用途。

卢比奥授权根据特朗普 1 月 9 日发布的一项行政命令支付这笔资金。总统的命令指出，这笔资金是美国以托管身份持有的委内瑞拉政府的财产。
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于财经市场信号，适合用于观察利率、汇率、股债商品、金融机构和宏观政策变化。
